## Purpose

Integration decides when verified task branches land on their feature branch and when a feature is ready for its pull request, so that each idea reaches the primary branch through its own feature (G3) and no landing overwrites other work (G2). It serves the operator, who merges 1 tested pull request per feature, and the sub-orchestrator, which gets conflicts as resolver tasks. It finds conflicts between features early by trial merges and keeps each feature branch rebased. It does not verify tasks (task-execution) and does not remove worktrees or write rescue refs (worktree-custody).

## Strategic classification

| Domain | Business model | Evolution |
|---|---|---|
| core | cost-reducer | custom |

_Strategize rationale_: core - G3 (each idea reaches the primary branch through its feature) depends on it, and G2 on its no-loss branch invariants; today's alternatives are hand reconciliation of task branches and hosted merge queues, which work on pull requests to a protected base, not on local task branches, and find no conflicts between in-flight features; rule 2 (diff >= 7); cplx 8 from bundles behind the fast gate, bisection, trial merges, stacking with resolver tasks and continuous rebases. — _future_: Core, not decisive (diff 7). Feature and task-branch aggregates own the landing state machine and the no-loss rows 04 F5, F7, F9, F11, L5, L9. If a hosted merge queue later supports local branches, the bundle and bisect part can become supporting (table-stakes former core); trial merges and stacking stay core (bet B2).

## Domain roles

**execution-context** — It owns the task-branch and feature aggregates and the land lock, with state machines and the no-loss invariants I8 to I12. Only fleetd code and 2 operator commands act here; git and GitHub pass an internal anticorruption layer ([define A15]).

## Ubiquitous language

| Term | Meaning in this context | Avoid |
|---|---|---|
| **Feature** | 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request to the primary branch, holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas (understand N2). The feature aggregate owns feature-opened to feature-merged (discover N2) | project, epic |
| **Feature Branch** | The branch of 1 feature that collects its landed task branches and reaches the primary branch through 1 pull request | integration branch |
| **Task Branch** | The branch of 1 task that lands on its feature branch through the landing state machine | worker branch |
| **Primary Branch** | The base branch of a project; main in this repository, not in every project | main, master, trunk |
| **Bundle** | 1 candidate made from the feature branch tip plus every ready task branch of that feature, tested once by the fast gate | batch, merge train |
| **Fast Gate** | The declared unit-test command of a project that every bundle and every rebased feature branch must pass | CI, check |
| **Full Gate** | The fast gate plus the end-to-end tests, run on a feature tip over the current primary branch; a pass goes stale when either tip moves | CI, e2e run |
| **Trial Merge** | A merge-tree result between 2 in-flight features, or a feature and the primary branch, recorded in the ledger with no checkout | dry run |
| **Resolver Task** | A code-kind task that resolves 1 conflict between stacked features, at most 100 changed lines or 2 files | merge task |
| **Ready** | A task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle. A feature is ready when its full gate passed and its pull request can open (discover N6) | — |
| **Landed** | A task branch state: the branch is fast-forwarded onto its feature branch after the fast gate passed (understand N4) | — |
| **Merged** | A feature fact read from git by content: the feature branch is in the primary branch (understand N4) | — |
| **Trial merge result** | The answer of a git merge-tree trial merge between 2 features, or a feature and the primary branch: clean, or the conflicting paths. Coined in connect (assumption A6) | — |

## Business decisions

1. A feature opens when its sub-orchestrator first writes assumptions, or when fleetd accepts a --direct idea; it gets 1 feature branch from the primary branch (understand N2, discover N2).
2. A task branch becomes ready only when its task is done (verified). Several ready task branches of 1 feature form 1 bundle on the feature branch tip in queue order; the fast gate runs once on it. No human approves a landing on a feature branch.
3. On a fast gate pass, the feature branch moves forward to the bundle by fast-forward only (I9). On a failure, fleetd bisects the bundle; the failing task branch goes to gate_failed and its triage task goes to the sub-orchestrator.
4. Under the land lock (1 h, 5 tries), just before the fast-forward, fleetd checks that the task is still landing and held by its worker; a cancelled task lands nothing (04 F9).
5. A red land after a rebase resets the branch to its tip from before the land (04 F7). A passed step stands only for the tree it judged; new commits reopen the land and every later step (04 F5).
6. Every git network call has a wall-clock bound: push 10 min, others 3 min, and it never retries (04 F11).
7. A task is landed, and a feature is merged, only when its changes are in the target branch by content, also after a squash merge (I8). Merged is read from git, not from the GitHub API ([define A19]).
8. Before each rebase or forced update of a branch, a rescue ref of the old tip exists (I10); worktree-custody writes it ([define Q6]). A fleet branch with no ledger row is adopted as an orphan row and reported, never deleted (I11). A branch is deleted only when landed, merged or rescued, and no git stash entry names it (I12).
9. When a feature tip or the primary branch moves, fleetd trial-merges each in-flight feature against the primary branch and every other in-flight feature with git merge-tree, no checkout. A conflict stacks the younger feature on the older one and opens 1 resolver task of at most 100 changed lines or 2 files (understand Q7).
10. When the primary branch moves, each feature branch rebases, bottom of a stack first, and the fast gate runs again; a rebase conflict opens a resolver task. The rebase does not wait for the running attempts of the feature; their task branches rebase at landing ([define A27]).
11. When every task of an idea is landed, the full gate runs on the feature tip over the current primary branch. A pass goes stale when either tip moves. A failure opens triage tasks of the feature.
12. A feature is ready only with a current full gate pass. Then its pull request opens: with pr gh through GitHub, with pr manual by a push and the compare URL. The operator merges by default.
13. A task branch parked by done --unlanded keeps its worktree, and unlanded work stays listed for a decision; a finding is decided once (04 L5, L9).
14. An escalated task branch is abandoned only by the operator; a rescue ref is kept, and the branch is dropped only after worktree-rescued (connect N4).
15. integration is the only caller of the git branch and merge commands: rebase, merge-tree, fast-forward, push and branch delete. It runs no git worktree command and writes no rescue ref; worktree-custody does ([define A26]).
16. integration and task-execution are a partnership: their 4 messages change together as versioned in-memory events (connect N6, [define A24]).

## Assumptions

- [understand A3] horch earns no revenue. Its value is operator throughput: approved ideas that reach the primary branch per unit of subscription usage. (confidence medium)
- [understand A4] The design gives no number for full use of the subscription usage. G4 uses a proxy: no pool ends its window with usage left while a task is ready, and a usage limit burns 0 attempts. (confidence low)
- [discover A6] The event order follows understand N7 (idea states), N8 (task branch states building, verifying, ready, in_bundle, landed with side states conflicted, gate_failed, abandoned) and N9 (worktree states reserved, created, active, landing, landed, orphaned, rescued, removed). (confidence high)
- [discover A7] 'Worktree landed' (nothing unique left) is folded into Task Branch Landed and Worktree Removed; it is not a separate event. (confidence medium)
- [discover A8] An idea with no --to gets its features row at capture and its feature branch at its first assumptions, so Feature Opened (the branch) happens after Assumptions Written (answer of the orchestrator, D15, to Q1 and H7). (confidence low)
- [discover A10] Event count 83 is above the standard band (25 to 60). The design has 4 state machines (idea, task, task branch, worktree) plus feature integration; merging them further hides the language conflicts H4 and H6. (confidence high)
- [discover A11] A state name is never written without the kind of its entity (design A20). The shared names stay: ready (task, task branch, feature) and landed (task branch, worktree). A task is done; its task branch is landed. (confidence high)
- [decompose A5] Worktree custody is its own context, not a part of integration, because the worktree lease and the no-loss rules differ from the branch landing rules. Decision D4, option A (orchestrator, D15). (confidence medium)
- [decompose A8] Triage and resolver tasks are opened by integration but run as normal tasks in task-execution; integration asks task-execution for them. (confidence high)
- [strategize A2] Core stays the minority: 2 of 6 subdomains (task-execution, integration). Ideas would make 3 of 6, which is half, not a minority (ticket rule for this run). (confidence medium)
- [connect A8] git is called by 2 contexts, split by concern: worktree-custody for worktrees and rescue refs, integration for branches, merges, bundles and trial merges (orchestrator, D15). (confidence high)
- [organise A4] The data store is 1 SQLite ledger (~/.horch/ledger.sqlite3, WAL) plus the workspace files, both owned by the 1 deployable. Inside the ledger each context owns its tables: ideas owns ideas, requirements, questions; task-execution owns tasks, task_deps, task_covers, attempts, leases; worktree-custody owns worktrees; integration owns features, branches, gate_runs, trial_merges; fleet-runtime owns events and ingested; worker-profiles owns no table (its profiles are teammate files). Source: design Ledger schema with the aggregates of discover and decompose. (confidence medium)
- [organise A5] The questions table belongs to ideas. decompose D2 option A (orchestrator, D15): worker questions belong to ideas, because the sub-orchestrator of the feature answers them. ideas also owns the 1 needs-you list (design OR-3; decompose N9). The sub-orchestrator answers through the command channel, and fleetd stays the only ledger writer. (confidence high)
- [organise A7] The cognitive load of core-team is high: 6 contexts and 2 core contexts (task-execution, integration). No second team exists to take a context, so the mitigation is module boundaries that an arch_scan rule enforces (orchestrator, D15), 1 context per task where possible, and the 9 migration phases (Phase 0, Phase P, Phases 1 to 7) that add the contexts one at a time (understand C9, N19). (confidence medium)
- [define A10] 'anticorruption-layer' guessed for external system git (core contexts protect their model; others conform) - confirm
- [define A11] 'anticorruption-layer' guessed for external system clock (core contexts protect their model; others conform) - confirm
- [define A15] git and GitHub pass an internal anticorruption layer.
- [define A19] pull-request-merged is only a hint; merged is read from git.
- [define A20] open-pull-request goes to GitHub only with pr gh.
- [define A16] Business model cost-reducer; decision D1 option A.
- [define A24] task-execution and integration are a partnership.
- [define A26] git has 2 callers: worktree-custody (worktrees, rescue refs) and integration (branches, merges).
- [define A27] Task branches rebase at landing.

## Verification metrics

- Business (G2): count of branches deleted while not landed, merged or rescued, or named by a git stash entry (I12). Target 0.
- Business (G3): count of features marked merged whose changes are not in the primary branch by content (I8). Target 0.
- Business (G3): share of landed task branches that hit a conflict. Baseline 2.7% of 376 (research-03 F7); target at most the baseline.
- Structural: count of feature branch or primary branch moves that are not a fast-forward to a gated candidate (I9). Target 0.

## Open questions

- [understand Q1] What number counts as full use of the subscription usage for G4: a share of each pool window consumed by its reset, or a count of ready tasks left waiting while a pool has usage?
- [understand Q7] Is 100 changed lines or 2 files the right size limit for a resolver task, and how accurate is a structural merge tool on the recorded conflicts of this repository?
- [understand Q8] This repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10), and plan validation refuses a project with no declared fast gate. Which command is the fast gate of this repository? Proposed answer (orchestrator, D15): the workspace tests without the crate horch-e2e. A run must confirm it.
- [discover H2 near feature-opened - conflict] 'Feature' is also a task kind (kind: feature, a code kind) and a word for any change. In fleetd a Feature is 1 sub-orchestrator, 1 feature branch and 1 pull request holding 1 main idea and its follow-on ideas. Which meaning does each document use (understand N2)?
- [discover H6 near task-branch-verified - conflict] 'Ready' names 3 states: a task is ready when its dependencies are done (not yet dispatched); a task branch is ready when it is verified and waits for a bundle; a feature is ready when its full gate passed. 'Landed' is both a task branch state and a worktree state. Which one does a status line mean? Answered (design A20): the state names stay, and each status line, event, log line and message that gives a state also gives the kind of its entity. A task is done; its task branch is landed.
- [discover H8 near task-branch-landed - risk] The Preservation analysis rows (04 W6, F9, F7, F5, L5, L9, W8, W9, F11, S7, L6, L8, S8, S10, M5, 05 E-10, 06 S1 to S15) are hard inputs. Each must have exactly 1 owner in the model; a row that falls between 2 owners is a behavior fleetd silently drops (understand N15).
- [discover H11 near fast-gate-passed - external] Plan validation refuses a project that has not declared a fast gate and a full gate, and this repository has no unit-only command today (research-03 F10, understand Q8). Until one is declared, no plan of this repository can commit.
- [discover H15 near pull-request-merged - external] A project setting says who merges a feature; the default is the operator. When the setting lets fleetd merge, which gate and which actor stands for the merge decision?
- [connect CC1 - coupling, high] task-execution and integration depend on each other: task-done and task-escalated go one way, task-branch-conflicted and resolver-task-opened go the other. Both are core, so a change in one state machine can force a change in the other.
- [connect CC3 - coupling, medium] ideas and integration depend on each other: assumptions-written and idea-tasks-landed go to integration, feature-opened, task-branch-landed and feature-merged come back.
- [connect CC6 - coupling, high] Trial merges, git worktree add and remove, and process starts are external calls. If one runs inside the ledger write transaction, a slow git or a hung process start holds the only writer.
- [connect CC7 - coupling, high] abandon-task-branch drops a task branch in integration, but the rescue ref that keeps the work is made in worktree-custody (04 W6). Both must happen, in order, or work is lost.
- [connect CC9 - coupling, low] task-branch-landed has 2 consumers that need different data: worktree-custody needs the task and worktree, ideas needs the feature and idea roll-up.
- [define Q6] Who writes the I10 rescue ref before a rebase.

## Quality attributes

| Attribute | Priority | Requirement | Scenario |
|---|---|---|---|
| integrity | high | No branch moves except by fast-forward to a gated candidate, and no branch is deleted unless landed, merged or rescued (I9, I10, I12). | When a bundle fails the fast gate after a rebase, then the feature branch stays at its old tip, the branch resets to its tip from before the land (04 F7), and a rescue ref of the old tip exists. |
| correctness | high | Landed and merged are read from git by content, also for a squash merge (I8). | When the operator squash-merges a feature's pull request, then on the next pass the feature becomes merged and its ideas close only after every worktree is removed. |
| availability | medium | A stalled git network call never holds the land lock for longer than its bound (04 F11). | When a git push stalls on the network, then it ends at 10 min (other calls at 3 min), is not retried, and the land lock is free for the next bundle. |
